questions.prompt: The window ____ by my father.
steps: The window receives the action, so use the passive voice.
Past passive = was/were + past participle; singular window takes was opened.

questions.prompt: I ____ my teeth every morning when I wake up.
steps: Every morning indicates a routine in the simple present.
With I, use the base form brush, without -s.

questions.prompt: I ____ the television when it started raining.
steps: Watching was in progress when another past event happened.
Use past continuous: I was + watching.

questions.prompt: The villagers ____ their environment at the moment.
steps: At the moment signals an action happening now.
Villagers is plural, so use are + cleaning.

questions.prompt: While they were playing, the teacher ____ swimming.
steps: Both activities were taking place in the past.
The teacher is singular, so was completes the past continuous.

questions.prompt: Mr Musa has been teaching at our school ____ ten years now.
steps: Ten years is a duration, not a starting date.
Use for with a duration; since introduces a starting point.

questions.prompt: We ____ to travel to Mtwara soon.
steps: Soon indicates a future plan.
The structure is are going to + base verb travel.

questions.prompt: I asked Juma if he could ____ me a piece of paper.
steps: Juma gives the paper temporarily to the speaker.
That direction is lend; could requires the base form, not lent.

questions.prompt: The fisherman has ____ a lot of fish.
steps: Has needs a past participle to form the present perfect.
The forms are catch, caught, caught.

questions.prompt: A cheetah normally ____ faster than a tiger.
steps: Normally describes a usual characteristic.
Singular a cheetah takes the simple-present form runs.

questions.prompt: We watched TV for ____ hour.
steps: Hour begins with a vowel sound because h is silent.
Use an before a vowel sound: an hour.

questions.prompt: I have to wake up early ____ be in school on time.
steps: The blank introduces the purpose of waking early.
So as to is followed by the base verb be.

questions.prompt: Many children like ivory sweets, ____?
steps: The statement is positive in the simple present.
Use a negative do-tag with plural they, and end the question tag with a question mark.

questions.prompt: I saw a cat in the bush. ____ cat was black in colour.
steps: The cat has already been introduced.
Use the for the particular cat the reader now knows.

questions.prompt: Chausiku does all the homework ____ she wants to be first in class.
steps: The second clause gives the reason for doing homework.
Because joins an action to its reason.

questions.prompt: The man ____ shirt was torn was in the academic office.
steps: The shirt belongs to the man.
Whose expresses possession in a relative clause.

questions.prompt: In our class, Jalia is ____ than Jamila.
steps: Than signals a comparison between two people.
Use the comparative shorter, rather than the superlative shortest.

questions.prompt: ____ you study hard, you are going to fail.
steps: The sentence warns of failure if the condition is not met.
Unless means if not: if you do not study hard, you will fail.

questions.prompt: Juma had ____ of time to prepare for his examination.
steps: The next word is of.
Plenty of is the correct expression for a large amount of time.

questions.prompt: Our class monitor put the English books ____ the table.
steps: Books rest on the upper surface of a table.
Use on for contact with a surface.

questions.prompt: ____ is hunger because of the poor rainfall.
steps: The sentence announces the existence of a situation.
There is is used to introduce a singular or uncountable noun.

questions.prompt: How ____ money do you need to buy a bus?
steps: Money is uncountable in this use.
Ask how much money, rather than how many money.

questions.prompt: You can go ____ to school or to the farm.
steps: The sentence offers two alternatives joined by or.
The paired construction is either ... or.

questions.prompt: Report Ally’s words: “I’m trying to get home in time.”
steps: Change I to he because Ally is now being reported.
After past said, the expected backshift changes am trying to was trying.
questions.answer: E — Ally said that he was trying to get home in time.

questions.prompt: This is the ____ news I have ever heard.
steps: Ever heard compares this news with all previous news.
Use the superlative best after the.

questions.prompt: Jane is a friend ____ I share the front desk.
steps: We share a desk with someone.
Keep with before the object relative pronoun whom.

questions.prompt: Has Maganga ever ____ off his bicycle?
steps: Has needs a past participle.
Fall has the forms fall, fell, fallen.

questions.prompt: Jane had to go ____ Anne because she was sick.
steps: The sentence describes accompanying Anne.
Go with someone means accompany that person.

questions.prompt: The headmaster switched ____ the television to watch the football match.
steps: The television must be operating to show the match.
Switch on means start a device; switch off means stop it.

questions.prompt: Is there ____ room for him to sleep in?
steps: This is a neutral question about the availability of space.
Any is the expected determiner in such a question.
questions.tip: Some or more can be grammatical in a suitably different context. Any is the intended neutral availability question in this exercise.

questions.prompt: What is the political leader of a country without a king or queen called in the choices?
steps: A monarch is a king or queen; a mayor leads a town or city.
President is the national leadership title intended among these options.

questions.prompt: The sister of your mother is your ____.
steps: Start from the family relationship: your mother’s sibling.
A female sibling of either parent is an aunt.

questions.prompt: A citizen of Sudan is a ____.
steps: The question asks for the nationality word.
Sudanese is used for a person from Sudan.

questions.prompt: A lady who is not married is called a ____ in the listed choices.
steps: Bachelor refers to an unmarried man; fiancée refers to an engaged woman.
Spinster is the older vocabulary term the examination expects.
questions.tip: For ordinary present-day writing, unmarried woman is usually a more natural description.

questions.prompt: Ali was first, John third, and I was ____.
steps: The three positions are first, second and third.
The remaining position is the ordinal second, not the number two.

questions.prompt: What is the opposite of forget?
steps: Forget means fail to recall.
Remember means keep or bring something to mind; retain the base verb form.

questions.prompt: Arrange: Take honey bees as an example.
steps: First introduce insects and then classify them as helpful or harmful.
Only after that general statement should a particular example be introduced.

questions.prompt: Arrange: They produce wax which can be used in many ways.
steps: They must refer to a group already named.
Honey bees are introduced in the third sentence, so this explanation follows it.

questions.prompt: Arrange: There are many kinds of insects around us.
steps: A composition starts by introducing its general topic.
This sentence names insects before later sentences refer to them.

questions.prompt: Arrange: Some of the insects are beneficial while others are harmful.
steps: The insects refers back to insects introduced in sentence 39.
It classifies them before sentence 37 gives a beneficial example.
questions.tip: Complete order: 39 → 40 → 37 → 38. Letters for questions 37–40: C, D, A, B.

questions.prompt: Which animal was cleverer than the Hare?
steps: The Hare ran fastest but did not notice a passenger on his tail.
The Chameleon used that advantage to reach the throne first.

questions.prompt: Which word in the story refers to runners in a race?
steps: Use the word actually present in the first sentence.
Contestants are those taking part in a competition.

questions.prompt: Where did the Frog and the Snake go to watch the race?
steps: The Frog proposed a place from which they could see clearly.
He specifically said to climb to the top of the hill.
questions.answer: A — To the top of the hill.

questions.prompt: The ____ ran fastest but ____ won the race.
steps: Separate running speed from the race result.
The Hare ran fastest; the Chameleon reached the seat first by riding on him.

questions.prompt: Which animal became King of the forest?
steps: The Hare claimed the title, but the Chameleon said he was already on the seat.
The celebrating friends recognised the Chameleon as the new king.

questions.prompt: Which animals were the happiest?
steps: Look for the pair described as happy at the result.
They celebrated the success of their friend, the Chameleon.
questions.answer: A — The Frog and the Snake.

questions.prompt: What did the winner of the race do?
steps: The winner rode on the Hare without the Hare noticing.
That was a trick, not evidence that he ran faster or bribed anyone.
questions.answer: C — He played a trick to win the race.

questions.prompt: Who were the Frog’s friends?
steps: The Frog watched together with the Snake.
He also called the Chameleon their friend.

questions.prompt: What does throne mean in the story?
steps: The Hare sat down on the throne.
The word names a royal seat, rather than the whole palace or racing ground.
questions.answer: D — The chair on which the king sits.

questions.prompt: Which is the best title among the choices?
steps: A suitable title covers the central event of the entire story.
The contest between the animals, with its surprising result, is the main event.

summaries.Section A — Grammar: Identify the time clue, subject and sentence structure before checking the options. For question tags, change a positive statement to a negative tag.
summaries.Section B — Vocabulary: Use the relationship or word class requested. Nationalities, family terms and ordinal numbers have distinct forms.
summaries.Section C — Composition: Start with the general subject, develop a category, introduce an example, then explain it. Check every pronoun has an earlier noun.
summaries.Section D — Comprehension: Distinguish what characters claim from the final outcome. Use details from the passage rather than assumptions about animal speed.
